newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-LOS ANGELES, D.C. UNITED ADVANCE TO MLS FINAL..
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LOS ANGELES, D.C. UNITED ADVANCE TO MLS FINAL..

text.p: - The Los Angeles Galaxy and D.C. United qualified for the Major League Soccer championship game by winning their respective conference titles over the weekend.

United was the first to clinch by defeating the Tampa Bay Mutiny 2-1 on Saturday to win the best-of-three Eastern Conference final series, two games to none. The Galaxy also won the Western Conference series in two games, edging the Kansas City 2-1 on Sunday.
The championship game will be played in Foxboro, Mass. on Sunday.

The Galaxy outlasted the Wiz in a shootout 3-1 after playing to a 1-1 tie in regulation in Kansas City. Preki had given Kansas City a 1-0 lead, putting in a rebound of his own penalty kick after he was pulled down in the penalty area by Greg Vanney in the 69th minute.
Vanney, a rookie defender, atoned for his mistake and equalised eight minutes later.

Salvadoran Mauricio Cienguegos converted the game-winning shot in the tie-breaker after teammates Robin Fraser and Vanney had scored. Paul Wright tallied for the Wiz. Los Angeles goalkeeper David Kramer, who replaced Jorge Campos in goal when the Mexican international went to forward in the 73rd minute, stopped shots by Preki and Mike Sorber and forced Mark Chung to shoot wide right.

Vanney, who finished with five goals in the regular season, connected for the game-winner in the Galaxy's 2-1 triumph in Pasadena, Calif. on Wednesday night. Chris Armas had lifted Los Angeles into a 1-0 lead in the 48th minute before Preki tied it several minutes later.

In Tampa on Saturday, Salvadoran Raul Diaz Arce broke a 1-1 tie in the 82nd minute to lift United to its fifth victory in six matches over the Mutiny, which captured the regular-season Eastern Conference title.

Rookie midfielder Steve Ralston had given Tampa Bay a 1-0 advantage in the 14th minute, but United drew even on a goal by defensive midfielder Richie Williams, who set up Arce's score in the 49th minute.

Arce recorded a hat-trick to power United to a 4-1 win in the series opener on Thursday in Washington, D.C. as the Mutiny played without both Colombian midfielder Carlos Valderrama and Canadian midfielder Frank Yallop, who had commitments to their respective national teams in World Cup qualifying matches.

After Arce and Tampa Bay's Roy Lassiter traded first-half goals, United broke the game open with three scores within a six-minute span. Steve Rammel snapped the 1-1 tie in the 54th minute before Arce put home a pair of insurance goals in the 58th and 60th minutes.
